name: Adaptive Refinement for Volume Rendering
definition: An interactive visualization method for sampled scalar functions of three spatial dimensions that uses adaptive refinement to balance rendering quality and performance. It starts with a coarse approximation and iteratively refines the image by casting additional rays in areas of high detail or error, leveraging the incremental nature of ray casting.
summary: Adaptive Refinement for Volume Rendering is an image-order technique that balances quality and performance by iteratively refining resolution based on local visual error, distinguishing itself by using hierarchical quadtree structures rather than neural fields or stochastic jittering.
